# Accepted Dependabot findings, with an expiry. Read by
# scripts/dependabot-alerts-gate.sh (#1074).
#
# Format, whitespace-separated, one per line:
#
#   GHSA-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx   YYYY-MM-DD   why this is accepted, and by whom
#
# THE EXPIRY IS MANDATORY AND IS CHECKED. An entry whose date has passed does
# NOT suppress the finding — the gate reports it as an EXPIRED acknowledgement
# and fails. This is the one thing `deny.toml`'s `[advisories] ignore` lacks: an
# ignore with no expiry is how an allowlist quietly becomes broader than anyone
# intended, which is exactly how `deny.toml` came to carry two
# `advisory-not-detected` entries matching no crate in the tree.
#
# Accepting a finding here is a RECORDED DECISION, not a deleted check: the
# alert is still printed on every run, with its GHSA id, severity, vulnerable
# range and first patched version, above a line saying it was suppressed.
#
# Prefer upgrading. Add an entry only when the fix is genuinely unavailable, and
# set the shortest expiry you can defend.

# (no accepted findings — the tree currently has zero open alerts)
